info.title: MICROSERVICE_PROD_Manage Webhook Endpoints API
info.description: The Manage Webhook Endpoints API allows businesses to control the lifecycle of webhook endpoints within their application. This API provides functionality to delete specific endpoints, enabling users to better manage their integration points for receiving real-time data updates. Typical consumers include developers integrating third-party services and maintaining system reliability by cleaning up unused webhook endpoints. By utilizing this API, users can ensure their systems are optimized for current operational needs.

delete.description: This operation allows you to delete a webhook endpoint identified by the resource ID. Once deleted, the endpoint will no longer receive events. Ensure that you have the necessary permissions to delete this resource.

requestBody.description: This request body contains the necessary parameters to delete a specific webhook endpoint identified by its unique resource ID. Ensure that the resource ID provided is correct to successfully delete the desired endpoint.

204.description: The webhook endpoint was successfully deleted with no additional content.

DeleteWebhookEndpointRes100045Request.description: A JSON string containing the request body for deleting a webhook endpoint.

DeleteWebhookEndpointRes100045Response_2.title: Webhook Response Metadata
DeleteWebhookEndpointRes100045Response_2.description: This schema represents the metadata for the webhook response after a DELETE operation.

WebhookResponseMetadata.title: Webhook Response Metadata Details

responseId.description: A unique identifier for the response.

correlationId.description: An identifier that correlates this response to the original request.

generatedAt.description: The timestamp when the response was generated.

processingRegion.description: The region where the processing occurred.

WebhookResponseMetadata.description: Contains details about the response metadata including identifiers and timestamps.

X-Endpoint-Id.description: A unique identifier for the endpoint that was invoked.

X-Runtime-App.description: The name of the application that handled the request.

bearerAuth.description: This security scheme uses Bearer Authentication to allow users to access the API. A JSON Web Token (JWT) must be provided in the Authorization header of the request. The JWT must be valid and properly signed.
